enableServiceLinks: false on every pod spec.

img-build-context.title: 5. How do I keep secrets out of the image?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-build-context-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. img-layers.title: 1. Why does every release push the whole app again?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-layers-1 · reproduced · baseline v0.1-b1 · 2026-10-17. The image built from the layered extract (extract --layers without --launcher, started with java -jar) has a usable AOT cache: -XX:AOTMode=on exits 0. Result: AOTMode=on with the image's GC and class path: exit 0 (openjdk version "25.0.4.1" 2026-08-18 LTS). Limitations: Proves the layout works with the AOT cache, not the layer sizes.
records.environment: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 x64 runner, Docker, images by digest from baseline v0.1-b1

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-layers-2 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. With the layered layout a code change only replaces the application jar and AOT cache layers; compressed sizes for one service were about 105 MB base, 48.5 MB dependencies, 0.1 MB application and 23.6 MB AOT cache. Limitations: Sizes come from the source guide's registry push of one service on linux/arm64.
records.reason: No test compares the layers of two builds yet.

img-non-root.title: 4. How do I run the app without root on a read-only disk?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-non-root-1 · reproduced · baseline v0.1-b1 · 2026-10-17. The image starts with a read-only root filesystem, /tmp as tmpfs, as UID 10001 and with an unreachable OTLP endpoint: /readyz answers 200 within 60 s. Result: read-only root, /tmp tmpfs, UID 10001, unreachable OTLP endpoint: /readyz 200 after 2.9 s. Limitations: Docker flags stand in for the pod security context; no cluster run yet.
records.environment: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 x64 runner, Docker, images by digest from baseline v0.1-b1

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-non-root-2 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Without a writable /tmp the embedded Tomcat fails to start with Unable to start web server. Limitations: Observed by the source guide with Spring Boot 4.1.1.
records.reason: No test starts the image without a writable /tmp yet.

img-pinning.title: 3. How do I stop the base image from changing under me?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-img-pinning-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Limitations: Documented Renovate and Dependabot behaviour.
records.reason: No test runs the update bots against the example service yet.

img-sbom.title: 6. How do I know which libraries an image ships?

Limitations: build depends on cyclonedxBom and the fixture workflow reads build/sbom/bom.json in the same run; that the SBOM is also packed into the jar is not checked.

checklist.text: Dockerfile with several stages; no JDK, Gradle or source code in the final image.
extract --layers without --launcher; layers copied dependencies, loader, snapshots, application.
AOT cache trained in the runtime stage with remote calls disabled; CI fails if -XX:AOTMode=on rejects it.
Base images pinned as tag@sha256:digest in plain FROM lines with the distro codename in the tag, auxiliary images included.
Every workload running the app image (Deployment, migration Job, CronJob) references the release digest, not a tag.
Renovate or Dependabot updates base digests and action SHAs; JDK major bumps blocked.
Numeric non-root USER 10001:10001 and exec form ENTRYPOINT.
Runs with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and /tmp as an emptyDir with a sizeLimit.
Allow list .dockerignore; no secrets through ARG or ENV.

Image SBOM (Syft, CycloneDX) attached as a signed attestation.
Trivy or Grype gate on fixable high and critical findings in CI; a registry or cluster scanner rescans shipped images.
Image signed by digest in CI; Deployments reference digests; an admission policy verifies the signature.

checklist.text: Connection budget computed: every pool times HPA maximum, surge and draining pods, plus migrations and admin, fits the user connections of each database server.
Fixed pool: maximum-pool-size equals minimum-idle, 10 or less unless measured otherwise.
connection-timeout between 2000 and 5000 ms, max-lifetime below every connection age cap, keepalive-time below network idle timeouts, leak-detection-threshold set.
spring.transaction.default-timeout and spring.jdbc.template.query-timeout set.
Runtime role has statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.
Separate migration and runtime users; the runtime user cannot change the schema.
Migrations run in a Job before the rollout; the application sets spring.liquibase.enabled to false.
Every schema change reviewed as expand and contract; no rename or drop in the same release as the code change.
Transactional changesets start with SET LOCAL lock_timeout; changesets that ran are never edited.
Integration tests run the real changelog on Testcontainers with the production PostgreSQL major version.
Alerts on hikaricp.connections.pending and hikaricp.connections.timeout.
Point in time restore rehearsed in the last quarter.

http-deadline.title: 4. Does a read timeout stop a slow call?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-deadline-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Apache's read timeout is inactivity between packets (a trickling response ran 4.1 s under a 1 s timeout) while the JDK client's is a deadline (the same response failed after 1.02 s). Limitations: Measured by the source guide against the Framework 7.0.9 and Boot 4.1.1 jars, not in this repository.
records.reason: No test runs this yet: the example service makes no outbound HTTP call.

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-deadline-2 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. The timeout of @Retryable stops new attempts but never interrupts one in flight, so the worst case is the timeout plus one attempt. Limitations: Reproduced by the source guide against Framework 7.0.9 through RetryTemplate and a proxied @Retryable method.
records.reason: No test runs this yet: the example service uses no retry.

http-idempotency.title: 6. How do I retry a payment without charging it twice?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-idempotency-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. A key passed as a method argument is sent unchanged on every attempt, because @Retryable invokes the method again with the same arguments. Limitations: Follows from how the retry interceptor works; no provider behaviour is tested. The Idempotency-Key header is an IETF draft.
records.reason: No test runs this yet: the example service makes no outbound HTTP call.

http-observability.title: 8. Why do some calls have no metrics or traces?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-observability-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Clients from Boot's RestClient.Builder or HTTP Service groups record http.client.requests and send traceparent; a client from RestClient.create() does neither. Limitations: From the Boot 4.1.1 auto-configuration (ObservationRestClientCustomizer) as read by the source guide.
records.reason: No test runs this yet: the example service makes no outbound HTTP call.

http-pool.title: 3. Why do calls wait minutes for a connection?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-pool-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Apache HttpClient 5.6 defaults to 25 connections in total, 5 per route and a 3 minute connection request timeout; Boot has no property for either. Limitations: Defaults read from httpclient5 5.6.4 by the source guide; the version Boot manages may differ.

http-retry.title: 5. When is it safe to retry?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-http-retry-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. A bare @Retryable retries any exception 3 times with a fixed 1 s delay and it does nothing without @EnableResilientMethods, which Boot 4.1 does not enable. Limitations: Annotation defaults read with javap on Framework 7.0.9 and Boot 4.1.1 jars by the source guide.

Limitations: Read from the Boot 4.1.1 configuration metadata by the source guide.

redirects dont-follow for calls between services, plus a status handler that rejects 3xx.
spring.http.clients connect-timeout and read-timeout set globally, tighter per group.
HTTP library chosen explicitly with spring.http.clients.imperative.factory.
Apache pool with maxConnPerRoute at or above the concurrency limit, a connection request timeout of 1 s or less and a connection TTL.
Each attempt is bounded by the client; the retry timeout plus one attempt fits the caller's own timeout.
@EnableResilientMethods present whenever @Retryable or @ConcurrencyLimit is used.
Every @Retryable sets includes, maxRetries of 2 or less, multiplier, jitter and timeout.
Only one layer in the call chain retries a given dependency.
POST and PATCH are retried only with an idempotency key created outside the retry.
@ConcurrencyLimit with policy REJECT on the class for each downstream system, rejection mapped to 503 or 429.
Circuit breaker or rate limiter only with a written reason, using resilience4j-spring-boot4.
Fallbacks never invent business results.
Clients come from Boot builders or HTTP Service groups, with histograms on http.client.requests.

spring.application.name, service.version and deployment.environment.name set.

Actuator on port 8081, exposure limited to health and info (plus prometheus when scraped), health details hidden.
No NetworkPolicy rule admits port 8081.

checklist.text: issuer-uri and audiences set; jws-algorithms explicit.
scp mapped to SCOPE_ and roles to ROLE_; oid as the principal; the API registration issues v2 tokens.
The API chain ends with anyRequest().denyAll(); business rules use @PreAuthorize; a catch-all handler rethrows security exceptions.
Stateless sessions; CSRF off only because no endpoint uses cookie authentication; CORS with exact origins or none.
Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy and HSTS present on responses through the ingress.
server.forward-headers-strategy pinned; server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies narrowed to the ingress addresses.
spring.web.error.* at defaults; spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled true; a catch-all handler returns a fixed text.
Validation 400s carry errors with field and message, never the rejected value; request sizes bounded on purpose.
URLs that users supply go through a client with InetAddressFilter.externalAddresses(), no redirects and https only.
Pod runs non-root with a read-only root filesystem and /tmp emptyDir, drops ALL capabilities, uses RuntimeDefault and mounts no service account token.
The namespace enforces Pod Security restricted; a NetworkPolicy denies by default with explicit allows and blocks 169.254.169.254.

vt-cpu-work.title: 4. Where does CPU heavy work go?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-cpu-work-1 · reproduced · baseline v0.1-b1 · 2026-10-17. With no CPU limit, -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1 overrides the CPU count the JVM detects, which also sets the number of carrier threads. Result: no CPU limit, nproc 2; -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1 reports Effective CPU Count: 1. Limitations: Proves the override only; the carrier count following it is from the JDK documentation.
records.environment: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 x64 runner, Docker, images by digest from baseline v0.1-b1

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-cpu-work-2 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. A virtual thread doing CPU work holds its carrier until it blocks, so CPU heavy requests starve the others. Limitations: From JEP 444 and the source guide.
records.reason: No CPU bound workload test runs yet.

vt-downstream-limits.title: 3. How do I keep a slow service from drowning in my calls?

vt-enable.title: 1. Should I turn on virtual threads?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-enable-1 · compiled · baseline v0.1-b1 · 2026-10-17. The example service builds and its Spring context starts with spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true. vt-executors.title: 5. Why does my @Async code still run on old threads?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-executors-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. A TaskExecutor bean declared by the application replaces the virtual thread executor Boot configures for @Async; spring.main.keep-alive keeps an app with no web server running. Limitations: From the Spring Boot 4.1 reference and configuration metadata.
records.reason: The example service has no @Async or @Scheduled code yet.

vt-fan-out.title: 7. How do I call two services at once with one deadline?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-fan-out-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Waiting on each Future with one shared deadline and cancelling late tasks returns within the deadline, while a try with resources executor waits for every task on close. Limitations: From the JDK 25 ExecutorService API and the source guide.
records.reason: No fan out test runs yet.

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-pinning-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. On JDK 25, synchronized no longer pins a virtual thread; JFR jdk.VirtualThreadPinned events show only native frames or class initialization. Limitations: From JEP 491 and the source guide.
records.reason: No JFR recording runs under load yet.

vt-resource-limits.title: 2. Why did latency get worse after I turned them on?

records.canonical: Evidence ev-vt-resource-limits-1 · not exercised · baseline v0.1-b1. Limitations: Reasoned from HikariCP behaviour and the source guide; server.tomcat.threads.max having no effect is from Boot's property description.

checklist.text: spring.threads.virtual.enabled is true only for I/O bound services; the decision is recorded.
HikariCP maximum-pool-size comes from the database connection budget; connection-timeout is 5 s or less.
Every downstream service has a concurrency limit (@ConcurrencyLimit, Semaphore or bulkhead) and every outbound call has connect and read timeouts.
CPU heavy work runs on a platform pool sized to the cores.
Pod CPU request of at least 1; either -XX:ActiveProcessorCount of at least 2 with no CPU limit or a CPU limit of at least 2.
No custom executor bean silently replaces the virtual thread @Async executor; spring.main.keep-alive is true for apps without a web server.
MDC, security and trace context are propagated across async boundaries; no business logic relies on ThreadLocal caching.
Fan out uses a long lived, context wrapped executor and cancels the tasks that miss the deadline.
A JFR pinning check runs once under load; dashboards show pool pending connections and GC.
